title: Senior's toolkit: Stryker.NET
summary: Install and run Stryker.NET, limit it to the files that changed, open the HTML report, fail CI below a score, and mark equivalent mutants in code.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: Stryker.NET
steps.body: Mutation testing runs your suite once per mutant, so it is slow on a whole solution. Seniors run it on the code that changed, and read the report rather than chase 100%.

toolkit.what: Install Stryker.NET as a .NET tool (or as a local tool in the repo's tool manifest, so CI and everyone use the same version).
flags: what CI runs before using it
toolkit.example:
dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install dotnet-stryker
dotnet tool restore

toolkit.what: Run from the test project's folder: build, mutate the project under test, run the tests per mutant, report.
flags: open the HTML report when done
toolkit.example:
cd tests/Shop.Tests
dotnet stryker -p Shop.csproj -m "**/Pricing/**/*.cs" -r html -o

toolkit.what: Only mutate code changed since a branch or commit: the way to run it on every pull request.
flags: exit non-zero if the score is below 70
mutation level: Basic, Standard, Advanced, Complete

toolkit.cmd: // Stryker disable once Equality : equivalent, i only counts up by 1
toolkit.what: Comments that switch mutators off for the next line, a block, or the rest of the file, with the reason a reviewer will read.
toolkit.example:
// Stryker disable once Equality : loop index, < and != are equivalent here
for (var i = 0; i < items.Count; i++) Process(items[i]);

toolkit.what: Commit the settings so local runs and CI agree.
flags: skip calls such as *Log* or ToString

steps.prompt: Match each need to the Stryker option.
pairs: mutate only what this pull request changed
fail the pipeline when the score drops under 70%
only the pricing code, not the whole service
see each survivor on its line in a browser

steps.prompt: A full Stryker run of the solution takes 40 minutes. How do teams usually make it practical?
options: Run it with `--since:main` on pull requests (minutes, only changed code), and a full run nightly or weekly
Run it only before a major release
steps.explain: Incremental runs give feedback where the new code is, which is where new untested behaviour comes from. The full run keeps the baseline honest.

steps.prompt: Run Stryker on the changed pricing code and fail below 75%.
steps.explain: `--since` limits the run to changed code, `--break-at` is the CI gate, and the HTML report is where you read the survivors.
